card.display_name: R39 style tilt / full / passive control
card.thesis: Round 39's passive control for the full slice, and the reason the matching tilt cell can be read at all. Slice: all seven traded names at once -- value, growth, core and the inflation-linked sleeve undivided. Entry 'close > 0' is true on every bar and exit 'close < 0' on none, with no stop, no target and no time stop, so this card buys all 7 name(s) at the window's open and holds them to its close at 0.12 each -- the same 84% capital budget every card in this field carries. It is a position, not a strategy, and it is in the field to be subtracted, never ranked or promoted. It does two jobs. Against its own tilt cell it isolates the timing rule, because the two differ in exactly one thing. Against the other three controls it measures the STYLE TILT ITSELF, which is this round's actual question and which no rule-driven cell can answer: value-passive minus growth-passive is the style spread, measured on identical windows through the identical engine. That quantity is what the scorecard cannot compute, because this harness scores every card against SPY, price-only and in USD -- and a value and mid-cap book measured that way over 2011-2026 inherits a decade of large-cap-growth leadership that no rule can overcome. Its discipline label is forced: ruleforms.classify returns None for a rule with no indicator in it and the Discipline enum has no member meaning 'passive', so 'trend' is the least wrong of seven wrong options and is not a claim about what this card does. It is a buy-and-hold proxy, not an index: it never rebalances, so it drifts away from equal weight across a long window, and it deploys 84% rather than 100%. The programme has never varied the style/factor axis: rounds 17 and 18 varied rule form on sectors, rounds 34-36 varied form, slot cap and fill order on industries and countries, and all of them returned margins inside the 21.2pp ordering-noise floor. This round holds the rule constant and varies the basket's style instead, which is the mirror image of every round before it. The hypothesis is the portfolio expression of a claim taken from this app's own influencer vault (persona wsaj: a ten-year US structural-stagnation view in which post-1982 tailwinds reverse and capital rotates away from mega-cap growth) -- a PROXY for a fundamental claim, not a test of it, because this repository has no fundamentals store and the persona's actual method is P/E and P/B relative valuation, which is unreachable here. No influencer is endorsed and the persona's own stated positioning disagrees with parts of this field. A factor ETF is also a bundle whose construction rules this round does not control: VTV is value because an index provider's screen says so, on a revision schedule invisible in these bars. This card is purpose=roth and every ticker it trades is absent from every savings- and trading-purpose card in the library, because Rev. Rul. 2008-5 destroys rather than defers a wash-sale loss whose replacement is bought inside an IRA. IAU sits in the pinned pool and is traded by nothing here: it is physical gold and the taxable book holds GLD, the textbook substantially-identical pair, and ticker disjointness is necessary but NOT sufficient under IRC section 1091 -- nothing here is a 1091-safety claim. VTI, RSP and SPYG all overlap the S&P 500 the taxable book trades through SPY: economically close, mechanically disjoint, and said out loud rather than left to be noticed. The benchmark is SPY, price-only, in USD, which is the wrong yardstick for a value and mid-cap book measured across a decade of large-cap-growth leadership -- that confound is pre-registered, and it is the entire reason each slice carries its own passive control so the round can report tilt-minus-control rather than tilt-versus-SPY. Not a proposal to trade anything. See strategy-program/ROUND-39-PLAN.md.
card.falsification: This card makes no claim about a rule that can be falsified -- that is what makes it a control. It carries one claim that can, and one way to fail. The claim: the passive value slice beats the passive growth slice by more than 21.2 percentage points on median exposure-adjusted excess over the eight main windows. That is the vault-derived style thesis stated as a number, it is falsified by any margin inside the floor or by the opposite sign, and it is predicted here to FAIL -- the honest prior is the programme's rounds 1-33 record plus a window mix dominated by large-cap-growth leadership. The way to fail: if this card does not hold all 7 name(s) on essentially every session of every window (session exposure at or near 1.0, one trade per name per window), it is not the passive baseline it is being used as, and every comparison drawn against it in this round is void. Its own worst window is gfc, trivially and by construction.
